where: crates/harness/mcp/src/typecheck.ts, first version in this lane
what: The type checker's TypeScript process was started lazily by the first cell that needed a check, inside that cell's async context, so the cell owned it: cancelling that cell killed the checker and the next cell was refused with `the type checker failed (Connection is closed.)`. No test showed it; I saw `Killed: pid … (…/@typescript/…)` in a real stop's reply while reading replies by hand.
cost: found by luck before anyone used it; fifteen minutes
cause: ownership follows AsyncLocalStorage, and anything started lazily inherits the context of whoever touched it first
whys: why possible: a process the kernel needs for its whole life was started on first use inside a cell
why not caught: every test started its checker outside a cell
property: 'whoever starts it owns it' applied to kernel-lifetime helpers
class: a kernel-lifetime resource created lazily in a cell's context is owned, and ended, by that cell
prevention: tasks.ts `outsideTask(fn)` runs kernel-owned work in no cell; the checker starts through it and is warmed at kernel start; typecheck.test.ts admits a cell from inside a task on a fresh checker and asserts the task owns nothing (it fails, naming the pid, when outsideTask is removed)
